title: Chamomile infusion for menstrual cramps
subtitle: A gentle cup for uterine cramping and pelvic tension
excerpt: A covered infusion of dried chamomile flowers steeped for ten minutes and drunk during the first couple of days of the menstrual cycle. Traditionally used for uterine cramping, pelvic tension, and the mild digestive upset that sometimes comes with a period. One cup takes ten minutes to prepare. Chamomile is in the daisy family, so patch-test first if you have had reactions to ragweed or similar plants.

glossaryTerms.definition: A hot-water preparation of leaves or flowers, steeped covered to retain the volatile oils. The herbal equivalent of making tea.

content.text: Chamomile infusion for menstrual cramps is a covered steep of dried chamomile flowers in just-off-the-boil water, drunk warm during the first one to two days of the menstrual cycle. Chamomile has been the western herbalist's first choice for cramping, digestive unease, and pelvic tension during a period for centuries. One to two teaspoons of dried flowers per cup steeped covered for ten minutes makes a pale gold, apple-scented tea. The cover matters: it keeps the aromatic oils in the cup where they do their work.

attrs.title: Precautions
attrs.body: Not medical advice. Consult a qualified herbalist or doctor for ongoing or serious symptoms. Chamomile is in the daisy family (Asteraceae). Readers with a known allergy to ragweed, daisies, chrysanthemums, or related plants should patch-test before drinking or consult an allergist first. No significant drug interactions at standard tea strength. Paediatric use: this infusion is prepared for adult women; for children, consult a paediatric herbalist.

items.prepNote: dried flowers; 1 tsp for a gentle cup, 2 tsp for a stronger one
just off the boil (about 95 degrees Celsius)

content.text: Warm the teapot or cup with a splash of hot water, then discard.
Add the dried chamomile flowers to a tea infuser or directly into the pot.
Pour over just-off-the-boil water. Cover with the lid at once.
Steep covered for 10 minutes. The water turns pale gold and the apple scent strengthens.
Strain into a cup. Drink warm.
One to two cups per day during the first two days of the menstrual cycle, when cramping tends to be strongest. Drink each cup freshly prepared. The
can be used for up to five days if discomfort persists across the cycle. If cramping is severe or not easing, see your GP rather than continuing with home remedies alone.

Dried chamomile flowers keep 12 months stored in a tin or jar with a tight-fitting lid, away from light, heat, and moisture. Prepare each cup fresh. Do not keep a brewed infusion for more than a few hours.
When not to use this remedy

Do not drink if you have a known allergy to plants in the daisy family (ragweed, chrysanthemums, daisies). See a GP for period pain that interferes with daily life, pain that has changed in character or become more severe than before, very heavy bleeding with large clots, pain between periods, or any period pain with fever. These can indicate conditions that need medical assessment rather than home herbal care.
